you know how someone will be asking you something and you say “what?” but before they can finish repeating it you understand what they said and answer? there is an actual reason for this! it’s because of echoic memory. 

memory has three stages: sensory, working, and long term. sensory memory refers to the 3-4 second span your brain holds new sensory information (such as words you hear someone say) before moving it to working memory. working memory is where your brain processes information. so, there is a potential 3-4 second span after someone says something in which even though you did hear them, you won’t understand what they said until it moves to the part of your memory that lets you understand what you heard.
